phases.buildUp: The centre-backs split while the deeper midfielder (RDM) drops between them to form a temporary back three. The full-backs stay low and narrow, prioritising security over progression. The goalkeeper is a safe short outlet but is happy to go long to the target striker when pressed. The aim is to invite pressure and survive the first line, not to dominate the ball.
phases.progression: Passes are vertical and quick. The CAM finds pockets between the opponent's midfield and defence and turns, while the box-to-box (LDM) drives forward. Width comes almost entirely from the wingers, who start narrow and burst wide to receive in space. Very little sideways passing — if the forward pass is not on, the ball goes long.
phases.finalThird: The striker pins the centre-backs and attacks crosses. The CAM arrives at the edge of the box, one winger attacks the far post and the other holds the width. The box-to-box midfielder supports from deep. Crosses and cut-backs are the primary channel, with quick combinations in transition when the opponent is unset.
phases.defensiveTransition: The first reaction is to drop, not to counter-press. The front four retreat into shape immediately and the double pivot screens. Only when a clear interception presents itself do the wingers and striker break at speed. The priority is to be compact before chasing the ball.
phases.defensiveShape: A narrow 4-4-2 out of possession with the CAM tucking into the wide midfield bank. The block sits deep, conceding the ball in front of the defence while protecting the box. Width is deliberately reduced to keep the centre congested, with the striker and CAM screening the opposition pivot.

phases.buildUp: The goalkeeper joins as an outfield player and the full-backs stretch high or invert. The single pivot drops to offer the first forward pass. Every player offers at least two passing angles, so the ball can circulate under pressure without risk. The aim is to draw the press and find the free man.
phases.progression: The mezzala and box-to-box midfielder alternate between the half-spaces. The pivot is the metronome, switching play from side to side. Width comes from the wingers who stay high and wide, forcing the opponent's midfield to cover impossible distances.
phases.finalThird: The false nine drops to drag centre-backs out and open the space behind. Both inside forwards attack the vacated space, and the mezzala arrives late. Chances come from overloads, cut-backs and quick one-twos around the box rather than crosses.
phases.defensiveTransition: Immediate six-second counter-press. The nearest three players swarm the ball, with the pivot cutting the forward pass. Rest defence is a compact 3-2 base. If the press is beaten, the team retreats into a 4-1-4-1 and rebuilds the block.
phases.defensiveShape: A high 4-1-4-1 with the line pushed up to compress the pitch. The single pivot screens centrally. Pressing traps direct play wide where the winger and full-back can pin the ball. The trade-off is space in behind, requiring a fast, aggressive back line.
